\begin{example} \end{example}[Einstein manifolds in dimensions 2 and 3]

↗ def:einstein-manifold ↗ def:sectional-curvature

If $n\in \{ 2,3\} $ and $(M^n,g)$ is Einstein with constant $\lambda $, then it has constant sectional curvature $\lambda /(n-1)$. \end{example}

Proof

\sketch ↗ def:einstein-manifold ↗ def:sectional-curvature ↗ def:ricci-curvature ↗ claim:curvature-symmetries-bianchi

For an orthonormal basis, write $K_{ij}$ for the sectional curvature of $\operatorname {span}(e_i,e_j)$. Then $\Ric (e_i,e_i)=\sum _{j\ne i}K_{ij}$. In dimension $2$ this gives $K_{12}=\lambda $. In dimension $3$, the three Einstein equations $K_{12}+K_{13}=K_{12}+K_{23}=K_{13}+K_{23}=\lambda $ force every $K_{ij}$ to equal $\lambda /2$.

□
